output.overview: Helix HX-5000 release 7.6 adds operational enhancements for EVPN control-plane maintenance, stack resilience, and multicast buffer visibility. The release also addresses a transceiver-related issue seen on 7.5 where QSFP28 uplinks could report intermittent loss of signal after DOM threshold recalculation. Overall quality focus in 7.6 is on improving stability in stacked deployments and reducing ambiguity in buffer-related troubleshooting, while maintaining configuration and forwarding behaviour compatible with the 7.5 train for typical core switching deployments.

features.name: EVPN route-refresh support
features.description: This release adds EVPN route-refresh handling so the routing process can re-advertise EVPN state without requiring a full control-plane reset. The feature is intended for operational use during route-policy changes and troubleshooting, and it preserves existing VXLAN/EVPN configuration. In environments with repeated route-refresh activity, monitor process memory until the follow-on fix is available in a later release.

features.name: stack heartbeat refinements
features.description: Stack heartbeat processing has been refined to reduce false separation events caused by transient jitter on the interconnect path. The change improves detection and recovery behaviour for stacked HX-5000 systems and adjusts internal timers used for dual-path heartbeat evaluation. No configuration changes are required, but TAC recommends verifying stack health after upgrade with 'show stack' in environments using long cable runs.

features.name: multicast buffer accounting
features.description: This release improves multicast buffer accounting so counters better reflect actual queue consumption during periods of sustained replication. The updated accounting is intended to improve troubleshooting of buffer drops and multicast congestion without changing forwarding policy. Existing multicast and QoS configuration is retained, but operators may notice counter values differ from earlier releases because the accounting model has been corrected.

output.compatibility: Release 7.6 is supported for upgrade from HX-5000 7.5. Configuration is expected to be forward-compatible with 7.5 for switching, stacking, spanning tree, LACP, and VXLAN/EVPN deployments, with no mandatory configuration migration steps. Mixed-version operation is not recommended for extended periods in stacked or EVPN environments, and the known issues listed for this release should be considered when planning maintenance on systems with long stack cabling or heavy EVPN route-refresh usage. Optical hardware and transceiver support remain aligned with the 7.5 hardware matrix; verify optics with 'show interfaces transceiver detail' after upgrade if the environment previously showed DOM or LOS anomalies.
upgrade_steps: Back up the running configuration and capture a copy of the current software image, stack state, and relevant operational output such as 'show stack' and 'show interfaces transceiver detail'.
Verify the 7.6 image checksum and digital signature on the staging server or transfer source before copying it to the switch.
Schedule a maintenance window that accounts for control-plane restart time and, if applicable, the time needed to upgrade stack members in sequence.

Install the 7.6 image on the standby or non-active system first, then reload or fail over according to the site upgrade procedure; for stacked systems, upgrade one member at a time where operationally permitted.
After the upgrade, confirm platform health with 'show stack', check interface and transceiver status, and validate EVPN, spanning tree, and LACP adjacency state as appropriate for the deployment.
Review system logs for unexpected warnings or process restarts, then save the confirmed working configuration if no anomalies are observed.
